Every programming language in the Marnov.why: The Marnoval family is made up: no family of programming languages by that name exists, and no text states this. The class above (programming languages) is real, and the new conclusion (dynamically typed) is the one the revised rule gives, so the record tests acquiring a new rule for an unknown family, one that could exist unrecorded among the many small research languages.

Sivane is dynamically typed..why: Made up, so stated nowhere: nobody writes a fact about something that does not exist. It follows only from the inserted rule and the membership given in the prompt, which is how people state things about a member of a group: through its group.

Type errors in Tolvec programs are not c.why: Made up, so stated nowhere: nobody writes a fact about something that does not exist. It follows only from the inserted rule and the membership given in the prompt, which is how people state things about a member of a group: through its group. That type errors surface at run time rather than compile time is the usual way people describe a dynamically typed language.

The Marnoval family and Python are both.why: Nobody compares the typing of a made-up family of languages with Python. What people do say is that Python is dynamically typed; the comparison follows only from the inserted rule and that fact.

Python is dynamically typed..why: Python's dynamic typing is stated in nearly every description of the language.
